title: fix(core): a gate declared with no evaluable source is a fault in its key's direction, not "no gate" (objectui#11358)
body:
Fixes #11358
Clause-②: yes

Runtime half of triage's ruling `5928128796` on objectui#11358: a gate value that is **present but has no evaluable `source`** — an `ast`-only envelope, `0`, `{}`, an array — is **declared and faulting**, never "no gate". Absent (`undefined` / `null` / `''` / blank text) stays "not declared". One definition, so the row menu, the toolbars and the selection bar change together. The `object-grid` door (`bulkActionDefs` unmirrored in `ObjectGridSchema`) is untouched, per the ruling's point 2 (objectui#6152 / objectui#11276).

## What changed, and where it landed

The three states are told apart in **one** place, a new internal module `packages/core/src/evaluator/unevaluablePredicate.ts` (`isUnevaluablePredicate` + the `[unevaluable]` reason). It is **not** re-exported from the package entry. Its four readers are all in `@object-ui/core`:

- **Normalizer** (`predicateInput.ts`): `toPredicateInput` no longer folds such a value into `undefined` (absent). It returns a frozen `cel` envelope with no `source`. `hasDeclaredPredicate`'s **code is unchanged**: `toPredicateInput(x) !== undefined` now answers "declared" for it, so the definition stays derived from the normalizer, with no second list.
- **Evaluation step** (`ExpressionEvaluator.evaluateCondition`): the value is a **fault**. A `throwOnError` caller gets a throw, so its catch is its fail-closed answer and its one report. Any other caller gets the fail-soft `true` plus one report through `evalFieldPredicate`'s channel (or the caller's `onFault`). This also removes the evaluator's own silent `true` for raw junk (`!condition` / `Boolean(condition)`).
- **`evalFieldPredicate`** (`fieldRules.ts`): tags the `[unevaluable]` reason beside `[blank]` instead of sending the value to the engine. The engine answered `AST-only evaluation not yet supported; persist source` even for a `0`.
- **Dev-mode validator** (`schema-validator.ts`): still **refuses** these values on `visible` / `disabled`. It now asks `!isUnevaluablePredicate(v) && hasDeclaredPredicate(v)`. Asking "declared" alone would have widened its accept set to exactly the shapes this card stops.

**Why the landing point is wider than `declaredPredicate.ts`:** the fold lived in the normalizer. Every toolbar `visible` leg evaluates `useCondition(toPredicateInput(raw), …, { throwOnError: true })`, so after `toPredicateInput` folded the value to `undefined`, the evaluator answered `true` and the action showed. Changing `hasDeclaredPredicate` alone would have hidden nothing on the toolbars. Each key's polarity also differs: on `disabled` / `hidden` the closed side is `true`, on `visible` it is `false`. So the fault has to reach the evaluation step, where each reader's existing fault policy carries the polarity. No reader outside core changed code. Outside core, only comments that this change made false were edited: `components` `visibility-gate.ts` / `data-table.tsx`, `app-shell` `ActionParamDialog.tsx`, `types` `expression.ts`.

## Every reader, and its new answer

Enumerated with `git grep -n -E 'hasDeclaredPredicate|hasDeclaredVisibilityGate'` plus the `toPredicateInput(` call sites, at base `3ae9193` (re-checked after merging `main` at `0a78a20`: no new readers).

| Reader (key) | Before, for these shapes | After | Pinned in |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `action:button` / `action:icon` / `action:group` members / `action:menu` items, `DeclaredActionsBar`, `RelatedList` toolbar, `useNavRunAction`: `visible` (`throwOnError`) | shown, silent | **hidden**, one report naming the action | `action-empty-predicate-scope.test.tsx`, `action-bar-member-visible-gate.test.tsx`, `actionPredicate.parity.test.tsx` |
| `ActionEngine.getActionsForLocation` `visible` | shown | **hidden**, one `warnHiddenPredicate` | `ActionEngine.visibility.test.ts` |
| Row menu: `isCustomRowActionVisible` (data-table, plugin-grid `RowActionMenu` item, inline button, "⋮" guard) | shown | **hidden**, one report | `RowActionMenu.test.tsx` |
| Selection bar: `hasVisibilityGate` / `partitionBulkRows` | offered, ran over **every** selected record | **no record qualifies** (bar hides the def), one report naming the def | `bulkEligibility.test.ts`, `specExpressionWire-10946.test.tsx` |
| `auto-trigger` (reads the leaf's `isVisible`) | would auto-run | refused, as any hidden action | via the `visible` leg |
| `disabled` legs: action leaves, `DeclaredActionsBar`, `record-quick-actions`, row items (`fallback: true`) | enabled | **disabled**, reported | `action-empty-predicate-scope.test.tsx`, `RowActionMenu.test.tsx` |
| `ActionRunner` `disabled` | ran | **refused** (`Action is disabled`), reported | `ActionRunner.disabledGate.test.ts` |
| `SchemaRenderer` `hidden` / `hiddenOn` | rendered | **hidden**, reported | `SchemaRenderer.hiddenDeclaredGate.test.tsx` |
| `SchemaRenderer` `disabled` / `disabledOn` | enabled | **disabled**, reported | `SchemaRenderer.disabledDeclaredGate.test.tsx` |
| `ActionRunner` `condition` | ran, silent | ran, **reported** (fork 1) | `ActionRunner.conditionGate.test.ts` |
| legacy `enabled` legs | enabled | enabled, **reported** (fork 1) | `action-empty-predicate-scope.test.tsx` |
| `filterVisibleParams` param `visible` (`fallback: true`) | shown | shown, **reported**, naming the param (fork 1) | `ActionParamDialog.test.tsx` |
| `schema-validator` `predicateGateRule` | refused | refused (unchanged) | `predicate-valued-gate-rules.test.ts` |
| `SchemaRenderer` `winningVisibilityKey` (diagnostic only) | skipped | names the declared hide key, as `shouldHide` now evaluates it | — |
| **Normalizer-only readers** (ask no definition): `action:bar` / `action:group` / `action:menu` own `visible` (`throwOnError`) | shown | **hidden**, reported | `action-bar-member-visible-gate.test.tsx` (the bar) |
| `record:alert` `visible`, `SchemaRenderer` `visible*` legs (fail-soft) | shown, silent | shown, reported | — |

Ruling pins: each faulting shape hides on all three surfaces with one report (toolbar, row menu, selection bar rows above). The absent control shows, and a real CEL `source` evaluates as before (the `controls` cases in each block).

**"One report"**, as built: once per evaluation path. A `throwOnError` leg reports through its own catch (deduped per label). The row and bulk folds report through `warnEvalError` (deduped per label). Fail-soft legs report through `evalFieldPredicate`'s channel under one fixed locator, so that last report is once per app for the whole class. That is the same limit the `[blank]` report documents. `hasDeclaredPredicate` itself reports nothing for this class: every declared gate goes on to an evaluation, and two reports for one fault is the noise objectstack-ai/objectstack#5149 removed.

## Fork 1: where the mechanism disagrees with the dispatch hypothesis (not chosen here)

The dispatch hypothesised fail-closed at **every** reader, including "not run for a condition". As measured, the change yields **each key's existing fault direction**: closed for `visible` (objectui#11212), `disabled` (objectui#11242) and `hidden`. On three keys a fault takes the open direction:

- a `condition` that faults lets the action run;
- a legacy `enabled` that faults leaves the control enabled;
- a param `visible` that faults shows the param.

On those three, junk keeps its old verdict and is now reported. Making junk closed there while a typo'd CEL stays open would put two fault policies on one key. Moving the whole key would also move every typo'd `condition`. Neither is this card's to choose. The options and their trade-offs are in the dev report on the card.

## Pull (who writes these shapes today)

- objectui `examples docs content skills apps` + non-test `packages/*/src`, gate key followed by a number, `{}` or `[`: 4 hits, **all comments, 0 producers**. Control: a boolean literal on the same keys gives 70 hits.
- objectui `examples docs content skills apps`, an `ast` key: **0**. Control: a `dialect` key gives 8.
- objectstack `examples` (shared checkout at `fbcc05f`), both queries: **0**. Control: a string or boolean literal on `visible` / `disabled` gives 15.

So nothing authored here starts hiding. The reach stays the one the card names: AI-authored metadata through the unmirrored `object-grid` door.

## Verification (head `e5b9458`, after merging `main`)

- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/core/ packages/plugin-grid/`: **372 files, 5511 passed**, 27 skipped.
- `pnpm exec vitest run` over `components` `renderers/action/` + `renderers/complex/`, the `react` / `app-shell` / `plugin-detail` / `types` suites that import the definition: **68 files, 1063 passed**.
- `type-check`: `core`, `types`, `react`, `components`, `plugin-grid` all exit 0 at `e5b9458`. `app-shell` exited 0 at `968766b`, before the merge, and was not re-run.
- `check:new-line-citations` (0 new), `check:control-bytes`, `check:action-forward-parity`, `changeset:check`, `check:changeset-claims`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check:esm-specifiers`, `check:unreferenced-sources`, `check:spec-symbols`, `check:test-path-roots`, `check:vi-mock-*`, `check:self-import`, `check-changeset-presence`: all exit 0. `check-governed-queue-guard --test` on all 29 paths: **NOT GOVERNED**.
- Not measured: `check:readme-exports` (exit 1 is "could not be judged": unbuilt plugin dists, outside this diff) and `check:node-esm-load` (it runs a full turbo build that did not fit the foreground cap). Core's built `dist/index.js` does load under node ESM: the probe below imports it.
- eslint, narrowed to the 28 changed `.ts` / `.tsx` files, in the form the package `lint` scripts run (`eslint .`, inline config honoured): **0 errors**. The checked set is the files git lists for this diff; the JSON output lists 28 files. The config sets no `parserOptions.project` / `projectService`, so type-aware linting is off, and this diff cannot move a verdict on an untouched file.

**Probe at base `3ae9193`** (hypothesis 1, confirmed): for each of the four shapes, `hasDeclaredPredicate` returned `false`, `toPredicateInput` returned `undefined`, and the definition printed **0** reports.

**Reverse verification** (committed first; mutation through `ablation-replace.mjs` with a `trap` restore). Deleting the one `isUnevaluablePredicate` line from `toPredicateInput` was predicted to turn red exactly these 34 cases, and did:

- core: the objectui#11358 block (4 shapes × 3) and the 5 rows marked objectui#11358 in the scope table;
- plugin-grid: the bulk block (4 × 2);
- components: the identity case and 4 `visible` + 4 `disabled` rows.

These stayed green, as predicted: "reports nothing", the derivation case, every control, and the `enabled` junk rows (same verdict either way). Run: `34 failed | 77 passed`. The restore was confirmed: blob `1ba52d1f` equals `HEAD`, and `git diff HEAD` is empty.

## Semver

`.changeset/11358-declared-gate-fails-closed.md`: `@object-ui/core` **minor** (AGENTS.md §9: objectui's own breaking change is marked minor). The breaking part: a gate written with one of these shapes now hides or greys out where it used to show. Note for the seat: `EvaluatorPredicateInput`, an exported **output** type, gains a member (the `cel` envelope with no `source`). No accept set widens and no export is added. The seat decided `Clause-②: yes` (claim amendment `5935805956` on objectui#11358): the exported union grows, so the published surface does. Line 2 above carries it, and the at-tier contract review `5936058554` passed on this head.

## Acceptance notes

- **Report dedupe for object-valued predicates.** Three diagnostics print a source-less object as one text, so two different junk shapes on the same node/key (or label) report once: `reportUnresolvableVisibilityPredicate` (`String(raw)`), `useCondition`'s catch (`label::[object Object]`) and `evalRowPredicate` (`(expression)`). The reports are weak, not wrong. Observation only; carrier: none.
- **A pending changeset's text.** `.changeset/6505-predicate-valued-gate-rules.md` (unreleased) still describes the validator drift pin as `boolean || hasDeclaredPredicate(value)`. `check:changeset-claims` lists it, report-only. It was true of that change, and it is left as written.
- **Toolchain.** The container's node `22.22.0` is below jsdom 30's engine floor (`22.22.2`), so the worktree was installed with `--config.engine-strict=false`. The sibling worktrees in this container carry the same install.
